summary: Term begins (20 Jan); returns to ‘Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon’; low direct signal.
Reimposes maximum pressure; ‘drive oil exports to zero’; ‘all options on the table.’
Letter to Khamenei with a ~60-day deadline; warns a military option ‘would be a terrible thing.’
First indirect talks (Oman/Rome) ‘constructive’; floats meeting Khamenei.
Hardens on ‘zero enrichment’ red line; ‘serious consequences’ warning; claims a deal is ‘close.’
Orders strikes on Fordow/Natanz/Isfahan (21–22 Jun); ‘obliterated’; then declares a ceasefire (24 Jun).
‘Peace through strength’; aggressive oil-sanctions enforcement (~115 entities, 30 Jul); talks dormant.
Continued pressure; backs the E3 snapback while leaving the door open.
Low-signal month; pressure-plus-openness as snapback mechanics dominate.
‘Ready to reach an agreement with Iran’ (13 Oct); optimistic tone.
Low-signal; the diplomatic opening lingers without a framework.
Reverts to ‘zero enrichment’/full dismantlement as Iran’s unrest grows.
Cancels meetings amid the protests; ‘help is on its way’; surges naval forces.
10-day ultimatum (20 Feb); launches Operation Epic Fury (28 Feb); talks suspended.
Peak war rhetoric: ‘UNCONDITIONAL SURRENDER’; infrastructure threats; brief oil-sanctions easing (~20 Mar).
Coercive diplomacy: short ceasefires, failed Islamabad talks, then a naval blockade (13 Apr).
‘Negotiating on fumes’; claims a settlement is ‘largely negotiated’ while running ~25 May ‘defensive’ strikes.
Backed a negotiated settlement amid Trump’s max-pressure; UK ‘focused on supporting the political process.’
Urged ‘restraint, calm and a return to diplomacy’; declined to join the US strikes.
UK (with France/Germany) triggered the UN snapback (28 Aug), citing Iran’s ‘significant non-performance.’
UN sanctions reimposed; UK added measures on 70+ Iranian individuals/entities (29 Sep).
Joined the 9 Jan E3 statement condemning the protest crackdown; moved toward IRGC sanctions.
After Epic Fury, ‘not involved’ but UK planes ‘in the sky’ for a defensive op; condemned Iran’s attacks.
UK announced ‘defensive military action’ (1 Mar); joined E3 condemnation of Iran’s ‘indiscriminate’ attacks.
Welcomed the 8 Apr ceasefire; priorities: reopen Hormuz and curb the nuclear/missile programmes.
Condemned Iran’s strikes on UAE oil infrastructure; urged meaningful negotiations.
Welcomed the 24 Jun ceasefire; ‘dialogue, diplomacy and de-escalation.’
Expelled Iran’s ambassador (26 Aug), suspended the Tehran embassy, pledged to list the IRGC.
Listed the IRGC as a state sponsor of terrorism (27 Nov); Wong: ‘acts of aggression… on Australian soil.’
Fresh sanctions over the protest crackdown (‘horrific use of violence’).
28 Feb joint statement: ‘Australia stands with the brave people of Iran’; Iran ‘a destabilising force.’
Backed the US/Israel effort but ruled out ground troops; deployed defensive assets to the UAE; demanded clarity on objectives.
Canada broadened Iran sanctions-listing criteria (6 Mar) across the handover.
Hosted G7 Kananaskis (16 Jun): Iran ‘principal source of regional instability’; urged ‘maximum restraint.’
Backed the snapback; implemented the reimposed UN sanctions (30 Sep).
More sanctions (14 Feb); 28 Feb backed the US ‘acting to prevent Iran obtaining a nuclear weapon.’
Walked back support ‘with regret’ (3 Mar) as ‘inconsistent with international law’; ‘Canada… will never participate.’
Co-signed the 8 Apr ceasefire statement; would support reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
Lobbied against US–Iran talks; threatened unilateral strikes; Trump warned him off.
Launched Operation Rising Lion (13 Jun); post-ceasefire claimed a ‘historic victory.’
Pressed Trump for a joint decapitation strike; Israel’s side of Epic Fury = ‘Roaring Lion.’
Sustained the joint air campaign; ground forces entered Lebanon after Hezbollah joined.
Welcomed the ceasefire but ‘not the end… a stop on the way’ to all objectives.
Wary acceptance of the deal track rather than new strikes (interpretive).
Reluctantly allowed indirect talks after Trump’s letter.
‘We are not seeking war, or nuclear weapons. We seek dialogue.’
pezeshkian_note: No Supreme Leader statement this month; block reflects President Pezeshkian.

summary: Dismissed US ‘control’ demands as ‘fantasy’; no surrender of enrichment.
Defiant post-ceasefire address (26 Jun); the pre-warned Al Udeid strike framed as calibrated retaliation.
Ruled out talks and an enrichment halt as snapback hit; called it ‘illegal.’
pezeshkian_note: Pezeshkian struck a softer tone at UNGA — ‘never sought a nuclear bomb’ (Cautious).

summary: Told Trump to ‘keep dreaming’ that the strikes destroyed the program.
Ordered a violent crackdown on the protests (casualty figures wildly disputed ⚠).
Killed 28 Feb in Epic Fury; Iran fired ~170 missiles in retaliation.
Installed ~8 Mar (59/88); first statement (12 Mar, read out — he did not appear) vowed revenge and to keep Hormuz closed.
Agreed (8 Apr, Pakistan-mediated) to a ceasefire and to reopen Hormuz; extended 21 Apr.
Negotiating a Hormuz/de-mining framework; Fars insists the strait stays ‘under Iran’s management’ (residual defiance).
Refused Saudi airspace/territory for the attack; condemned Israeli ‘aggressions against the brotherly Islamic Republic of Iran.’
Hosted FM Araghchi in Jeddah for ‘fruitful’ talks.
Authorized force against Iranian incursions but avoided joining the offensive (strategic restraint).
Denied use of Prince Sultan airbase for the US Hormuz escort mission; backed Pakistan diplomacy.
Supported the diplomatic Hormuz track (strong oil-market de-escalation incentive).
Backed US–Iran diplomacy with a hard edge: ‘nuclear experts around the table’ or ‘a more dangerous Iran.’
Call with FM Araghchi; stressed EU readiness to engage on the nuclear file.
‘Iran must not be allowed to develop a nuclear weapon’; urged all sides to step back; joined Geneva talks.
EU follows the UN snapback in reimposing sanctions; ‘must not be the end of diplomacy.’
EU condemned the crackdown; FAC (29 Jan) agreed to list the IRGC as terrorist + new measures.
Condemned Iran’s retaliation but distanced the EU: ‘This is not Europe’s war… We were not consulted.’
Welcomed the 8 Apr ceasefire as ‘a step back from the brink’; ‘the Strait of Hormuz must be open.’
Focused on Hormuz freedom of navigation (EU Aspides mission needs ‘more ships’).

Ordered new US strikes on Iran ~June 10 over stalled talks, threatened to 'take over' Hormuz and resume bombing during June 21 Switzerland talks, but also signed the Versailles MOU on June 17 to end the war — combining military escalation with deal-making
source: AP via PBS (Jun 21); NBC News (Jun 17); AP via Washington Post (Jun 10)

summary: Warmly welcomed US-Iran MOU on June 14 as 'hugely important step forward', pledged UK support for technical talks on nuclear issues and Hormuz; continued to advocate for diplomatic resolution while maintaining UK defensive military posture in region

Welcomed US-Iran agreement on June 15, called for restraint and constructive engagement; stressed importance of Hormuz reopening for Australian economy and urged Iran to address nuclear concerns through dialogue
source: Australian Minister for Foreign Affairs statement (Jun 15); SBS News (Jun 15)

summary: PM Carney called US-Iran deal a 'game changer' at G7 (Jun 16), offered Canada as third-party financial monitor for deal compliance; advocated diversifying energy supply away from Hormuz chokepoint

Defied Trump's call to halt strikes on June 8, hitting Iranian petrochemical plant; declared Israel's 'struggle is not over' and pledged to stay in Lebanon 'security zones'; ministers said Israel 'won't be bound' by US-Iran deal
source: NBC News / Reuters (Jun 8-9); Times of Israel (Jun 12); CNN (Jun 8)

summary: New Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei authorized the MOU despite stating he had 'a different opinion'; endorsed direct US talks while warning against US 'greed'; Pezeshkian signed the deal and displayed it publicly, showing more conciliatory posture than the supreme leader

Imposed first-ever EU freedom-of-navigation sanctions on IRGC entities over Hormuz blockade on June 8; called Iran's actions 'unacceptable' while urging all parties to return to negotiating table; EU welcomed MOU but refused to back regime change
source: EU press release via AP (Jun 8); Euronews (Mar 1); UANI digest (Jun 8)

summary: Declared ceasefire 'over' at NATO summit Jul 8; ordered 13 consecutive nights of strikes; reimposed oil sanctions; called Iran leaders 'cuckoo,' 'evil,' and 'scum.' Softened late-month, pausing strikes Jul 25-26 and saying Iran 'getting more serious' about talks.
source: CNN Jul 8 live blog; NPR Jul 8; CNN Jul 24-25 live blogs

summary: Condemned Iran's strikes on commercial shipping and Gulf partners; called for urgent ceasefire resumption Jul 13; government proscribed IRGC as terrorist organization; maintained UK 'not our war' line while warning of energy-price impact on UK households at NATO summit.
source: Anadolu Agency Jul 13; AA.com.tr NATO Jul 8; Reuters Jul 13

summary: Australian forces remain deployed but government distances itself from escalation; Albanese appeals to Trump over tariffs amid strike pause; energy supply concerns drive domestic debate.
source: Bloomberg Australia Briefing Jul 26; WSWS Jul 17

summary: Carney backed US strikes as 'appropriate' at NATO Ankara summit Jul 8 but stressed 'not a blank cheque'; visited Saudi Arabia Jul 9 to deepen ties amid ceasefire collapse; condemned Iranian attacks on Gulf shipping.
source: CBC News Jul 8; CBC News Jul 9; Global News

summary: Told Fox News Jul 26 the Iran war will end 'when the Iranian regime falls, or weakens to such an extent that it understands it must end its nuclear program'; vowed expanded operations; discussed 'all issues on the agenda including the situation in Iran' ahead of Trump meeting.
source: Jerusalem Post Jul 26; Times of Israel Jul 26; World Israel News Jul 26

summary: Under Mojtaba Khamenei (successor since Mar 8, not yet publicly appeared), Iran declared Strait of Hormuz closed Jul 11, struck commercial ships, attacked US bases across Bahrain/Kuwait/Jordan/Qatar/Syria, fired ballistic missiles at Aqaba. Pezeshkian divergence: president called for massive funeral turnout and earlier set conditions for ceasefire but state machinery continued escalation. An Iranian official dismissed Trump's late-month overtures, calling it 'a war that will not end.'
source: CNN Jul 11; Al Jazeera Jul 17; IranWire Jul 21; CNN Jul 25

summary: Saudi Arabia came under direct Iranian and Houthi attack in July; MBS had previously counseled Trump against strikes then urged ceasefire once war began; now pursuing security priorities while hosting Carney for economic talks amid ceasefire collapse.
source: House of Saud analysis; CBC Jul 9; AP/Bloomberg Jul 22-25

summary: EU High Rep Kallas posted Jul 25 criticizing Iran's repression of its own people and saying the regime pays a steep economic price for reckless actions; EASA warned airlines against Jordanian airspace. Iran slammed Kallas for 'hypocrisy.'
source: CBS News Jul 25; Tasnim News Agency Jul 25; Tehran Times Jul 25

summary: Canceled planned multi-day strikes on Iran (Aug 1) citing Gulf state requests, but then threatened to bomb Oman (Aug 17) if it 'gets in the way' of Hormuz talks, demanded compensation from Iran as precondition for negotiations (Aug 10), launched sweeping 'economic D-Day' sanctions (Aug 24), while saying he is 'not in a hurry' to reach a deal.
source: CNN live blogs Aug 1/10/17/24 2026; NBC News Aug 17 2026; Washington Post Aug 17 2026

summary: UK co-signed the 32-country statement condemning Iran executions (Aug 12) and maintained earlier position of not joining the US blockade or direct combat; continued to allow US use of UK bases while avoiding escalatory rhetoric.
source: Joint statement via German Foreign Office / Canada.ca Aug 12 2026; GlobalSecurity Day 181 report Aug 27 2026

summary: Australia co-signed the 32-country statement condemning Iran's executions (Aug 12) and maintained its limited military deployment, while continuing to advise Australians not to travel to Iran.
source: Joint statement Canada.ca Aug 12 2026; Australian Foreign Minister media release; IranWire Aug 12 2026

summary: Carney government sanctioned five Iranian officials for undermining international security via the Hormuz blockade (Aug 14) and co-signed the 32-country statement on executions, while continuing to officially abstain from the war.
source: CTV News Aug 14 2026; CBC News Aug 14 2026; Canada.ca joint statement Aug 12 2026

summary: Publicly stated he told Trump during their late-July Washington meeting to 'tighten the siege' on Iran via diplomacy, military action, and economic pressure; pushed for intensified secondary sanctions on Tehran's support networks.
source: Times of Israel Aug 26 2026; CNN Aug 26 2026; Japan Times Aug 25 2026

summary: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei appointed six top military commanders (Aug 11) including new IRGC chief, remained silent for days on Pezeshkian's peace push, and urged Gulf rulers to 'confront the real enemy.' Pezeshkian divergence: President called for end to 'no war, no peace' status (Aug 9) and endorsed renewed peace MoU (Aug 30), openly breaking with Khamenei's hardline posture.
source: IranWire Aug 11 2026; RFE/RL Aug 11 2026; Al Jazeera Aug 9 2026; NBC News Aug 30 2026; Gulf News Aug 30 2026; GlobalSecurity Day 181 report

summary: Signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement (Aug 7) with Turkey and Pakistan—a NATO-style mutual defense pact framed as 'purely defensive'—while avoiding directly naming Iran; Saudi Arabia continued to face Houthi attacks on its oil tankers.
source: Atlantic Council Aug 7 2026; PBS News Aug 7 2026; Iran International Aug 7 2026

summary: EU High Representative co-led the 32-country joint statement (Aug 12) condemning Iran's executions; continued EU sanctions posture targeting human rights violators while supporting diplomatic solutions.
source: Italian Foreign Ministry Aug 12 2026; IranWire Aug 12 2026; Consilium EU sanctions page

summary: On Sep 20 Fox News call, Trump laid out three paths for Iran: make a deal, 'let them rot economically,' or 'wiping Iran out entirely.' Continued authorizing major CENTCOM strikes including destruction of Iranian oil tankers and air defense targets throughout month.

NOTE: Starmer resigned Jun 22; Andy Burnham became UK PM Jul 20. Burnham continued allowing UK bases for US Iran strikes but faced anti-war protests. Planned first in-person Trump meeting at UNGA to discuss Hormuz shipping.

Australia remains militarily deployed in Persian Gulf but Albanese government continues to question conflict's endgame; navigating alliance commitments against domestic pressure over energy costs and open-ended involvement.

PM Mark Carney spoke with Trump 'a couple of times' about Iran conflict (Sep 10). Extended fuel tax break (Sep 2) to offset Iran-war energy costs. Canada formally condemned Iran's destabilizing actions (Sep 6). Did not rule out further involvement.

In Rosh Hashanah toast (Sep 6), Netanyahu declared 'the end of the Iranian regime is near' and vowed Israel would 'complete the mission of toppling the regime in Iran.' Called the regime weak and 'fighting for its life.'
source: jpost.com (Sep 6 2026); foxnews.com (Sep 6 2026); globalsecurity.org Israel PM statement (Sep 6 2026)

summary: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei made no public statement or appearance in September (none since taking office Mar 8). However, regime ordered massive Basij mobilization (330,000) in Tehran on Sep 18 in response to Kurdish unrest. Pezeshkian divergence: President Pezeshkian secured US visa and headed to UNGA (Sep 20-21), signaling diplomatic willingness despite regime's military posture.
source: globalsecurity.org Day 203 update (Sep 18 2026); congress.gov CRS R48887; cnbc.com (Sep 21 2026); tbsnews.net (Sep 20 2026)

summary: Saudi Arabia faced crisis as East-West pipeline was shut (Sep 11) after drone attacks from Iraq. MBS reportedly called Trump twice to request US strikes against Houthis. Kingdom navigating between coalition membership and direct Iranian/proxy threats to its infrastructure.

Kallas addressed European Parliament (Sep 15) warning of perilous escalation; announced new sanctions on 19 Iranian officials for human rights violations; pledged to reinforce EU ASPIDES naval operation and support Saudi-led maritime coalition. Called for end to repression and diplomatic resolution.
